input.description: A webhook will deliver a note's path and its content; for now just write it to disk exactly where it says, nothing fancier.

draft-workflow.name: save-note
draft-workflow.description: a webhook delivers a note's path and content; it is written to disk
draft-workflow.toml:
name = "save-note"
kind = "run"
description = "a webhook delivers a note's path and content; it is written to disk"

steps = [
  { action = "write-file", effect = "file" },
]

[trigger]
on = "webhook"
name = "save-note"

[assert]
written = ["bash", "-c", "grep -q '^file' \"$FORGE_EFFECT_LOG\""]

[limits]
budget_usd = 0.0
per_day = 100
on_failure = "ask:operator"
draft-workflow.rationale: The catalog's "write-file" operation is exactly this: it writes FORGE_INPUT_CONTENT to FORGE_INPUT_PATH and logs a file effect, honouring a dry run already. A webhook trigger is what "a webhook will deliver" names; the assert checks the file effect was logged. No new action needed.
open_questions: the webhook's own name ("save-note") is guessed from the description; the operator may want a different one
the per_day rate (100) and on_failure (ask:operator) are guessed defaults, since the description gave no rate or failure policy
budget_usd 0.0 assumes this step never calls a paid provider; confirm before raising it
